name: NMEA / Serial Log Parser
blurb: a serial log parsed line by line into a table of fields
intro: Parses a pasted serial log line by line. NMEA 0183 sentences are checksum-verified and decoded field by field (GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG, GLL, ZDA, TXT; other types listed raw), with the last fix and time span summarised. Other logs are read as CSV or key=value lines with per-field min/max/mean. Timestamps and debug text before a '$' are skipped.

examples.title: GPS module output with a debug line and one corrupted sentence

input.log:
t=1000 temp=23.4 hum=41 vbat=3.91
t=2000 temp=23.6 hum=41 vbat=3.90
t=3000 temp=24.1 hum=40 vbat=3.90
error: i2c nack
t=4000 temp=24.3 hum=39 vbat=3.89

usage: Give log as text (one sentence or record per line) and mode = auto, nmea, csv or kv. For NMEA it returns counts of good sentences and checksum errors, the talkers, last position in decimal degrees, fix/sats/HDOP, altitude, max speed and UTC span, one table per sentence type with decoded fields, a Problems table (bad checksum, non-NMEA lines) and a track CSV. For CSV or key=value it returns the rows as a table, min/max/mean per numeric field and a CSV export. Use it to check a GNSS module's output or to tabulate a device's serial telemetry.
sources: NMEA 0183 Standard v4.11, §5.2 (sentence structure and checksum) and sentence definitions GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG, GLL, ZDA, TXT
u-blox 8 / M8 Receiver Description and Protocol Specification, §31 (NMEA protocol, field meanings)
